stem: A bookshelf has 4 copies of the same novel, 3 copies of the same textbook, and 2 copies of the same dictionary. In how many distinct ways can all 9 books be arranged in a row on the shelf?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 9 books with 3 groups of identical copies: 4 novels, 3 textbooks, 2 dictionaries. Distinct arrangements = 9! / (4! x 3! x 2!) = 362880 / (24 x 6 x 2) = 362880 / 288 = 1260.
Computed 9! = 362880 as if all 9 books were distinct, ignoring that identical copies within each title are indistinguishable.

Divided 9! by 4! x 3! = 144 only, forgetting to divide by 2! = 2 for the identical dictionaries, giving 362880 / 144 = 2520. Or equivalently divided by 3! x 2! = 12 only (missing the 4! term), giving 362880 / 12 = 30240.

Computed 4! + 3! + 2! = 24 + 6 + 2 = 32 and then 9! / ... incorrectly, or treated each group independently as arrangements of identical objects (4-1)! x (3-1)! x (2-1)! = 6 x 2 x 1 = 12, arriving at a distorted small figure like 720 = 6!.

explanation: Total 9 books: 4 identical novels, 3 identical textbooks, 2 identical dictionaries. Distinct row arrangements = 9! / (4! x 3! x 2!) = 362880 / 288 = 1260.

explanation_sections.punchline: Three groups of identical objects each reduce the count: divide 9! by the product of all three group factorials (4! x 3! x 2!).
explanation_sections.approach: Name the formula: n! / (r1! x r2! x ... x rk!) for n objects with k groups of identical items. Map givens: n=9, r1=4 (novels), r2=3 (textbooks), r3=2 (dictionaries). Denominator = 24 x 6 x 2 = 288. Answer = 362880 / 288 = 1260.
explanation_sections.lesson: Each group of identical copies contributes one factorial to the denominator. With three groups you divide by three factorials multiplied together, not added.
explanation_sections.timing: 70-80 s. Compute denominator step by step: 4! = 24, 3! = 6, 2! = 2, product = 288. Then 362880 / 288 = 1260. Trap: forgetting any one group (e.g., stopping at 4! x 3! = 144 gives 2520, a plausible-looking wrong answer).
